component.name: Rail Narrator
component.summary: Reads PDFs aloud, highlighting each passage on the page and saying what the maths means

description.p: Rail Narrator reads a PDF aloud. While it reads, it highlights the passage being spoken in the page itself and keeps that passage in view. It is made for papers and technical documents: pointed at a language model, it says what an equation means rather than reading out its symbols.

ul.li: The passage being read highlighted where it is printed, word by word with a voice that times its words
Maths read for its meaning through a local language model or Claude, or read as notation by an on-device formula model
Running heads, footnotes, references, figures and contents pages skipped
Notes and highlights while you listen, kept beside the PDF and never written into it
A whole document narrated ahead of time, and an audiobook with chapters made from it
Speech, layout and formula models that run on your own computer

description.p: Keeps your place in a document when its narration is prepared again (after an update, a new layout model or changed filters), and opens a document with a saved narration sooner.
Fixes playback getting stuck or starting on its own after quick presses, edits and voice changes, and reads a lone letter "a" in maths as the letter rather than the article more reliably.
Fixes short freezes of the window: when changing the speed, when starting or replaying a passage, and when first opening the review notes.

Fixes from stress-testing: quick Play/Pause presses are no longer lost, keys are ignored while a file dialog is open, the status bar names the section being read, and the welcome screen and notices are tidier.
Fixes two playback problems: a long silence after skipping through many passages quickly, and reading stopping after the voice was changed several times in a row.
An AppImage for Linux and an installer for Windows, and Phonon's speech model downloadable from inside the application.
